title: Naturality of the localized stalk comparison into derived pullback
statement: Fix a cartesian square and its actual stalk algebra structures [def-pc-single-complex-base-change-stalk-condition]. Let P,Q be K-flat O_X-module complexes with invertible specified pullback counits, and let a:Q(P)≅Q(Q) be a derived isomorphism. Let e be a tensor-algebra-linear isomorphism between their model cohomologies whose restriction to B equals the canonical comparisonSourceUnderlyingIso [lem-pc-stalk-comparison-source-transport]. Define comparisonIntoPullback(P) by localizedComparison, homology of tensorStalkIso, the inverse exact-stalk cohomology identification, and cohomology of the inverse pullback counit. Its target is H^i of the derived stalk of L(g')^*Q(P). Then comparisonIntoPullback(P) followed by derived-stalk cohomology of L(g')^*(a) equals the C-extension of e followed by comparisonIntoPullback(Q). This holds for every point z and integer i, without a final target complex or morphism φ, base flatness, Tor-independence, or invertibility of localizedComparison.

proof.text: The K-flat stalk criterion makes the stalks of P and Q A-K-flat, so their ordinary A-to-C extensions compute A-derived extension. The degreewise tensorStalkIso identifies these complexes with stalks of ordinary sheaf pullback. Localize and use the universal derived pullback counits to identify them with the derived stalks of L(g')^*Q(P) and L(g')^*Q(Q).

The canonical transformation from base-derived tensor to A-derived extension comes from scalar extension and tensor associativity. Its chain-level naturality descends through localization, hence applies to a without a chain-map representative. Apply cohomology, and compare the two base-derived models by their unique counit-compatible identification. comparison_eq identifies their comparisons with the counits; localized_eq characterizes their scalar-extension transposes.

The tensorStalkIso components are fixed by the shared natural pullback-stalk isomorphism, so their cohomology identifications are natural. The localization factors are natural as well. Compose these equations with the inverse counits in comparisonIntoPullback. Faithfulness of restriction to B identifies the supplied e with the canonical transport. Extend e to C and use the adjunction equation to obtain the stated square.

theorem comparisonIntoPullback_naturality (z : X')
    (P Q : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (hP : P.IsKFlat) (hQ : Q.IsKFlat)
    (hcP : IsIso ((counit g').app ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ (.up ℤ)).obj P)))
    (hcQ : IsIso ((counit g').app ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ (.up ℤ)).obj Q)))
    (a : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj Q) (i : ℤ) :
    letI := leftAlgebra f g' z
    letI := rightAlgebra f f' g g' sq z
    letI := (tensorMap f f' g g' sq z).toAlgebra
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard (ModuleCat.{u} (R f g' z))
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard (ModuleCat.{u} (B f' z))
    ∀ e : (cohomologyModel f f' g g' sq z P).cohomology i ≅
        (cohomologyModel f f' g g' sq z Q).cohomology i,
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{u} Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight.toRingHom).map e.hom =
        (comparisonSourceUnderlyingIso f f' g g' sq z P Q a i).hom →
      comparisonIntoPullback f f' g g' sq z P hcP i ≫
        (comparisonStalkCohomology X' z i).map ((derivedPullback g').map a.hom) =
      (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, u}
        (algebraMap (A g' z ⊗[R f g' z] B f' z) (C z))).map e.hom ≫
        comparisonIntoPullback f f' g g' sq z Q hcQ i
